Even the time I stepped on a nail didn't hurt as badly as the common injection needle. I sometimes wondered if it was the insidious will behind it that made it hurt more. Point is,my pain detection was always hit or miss. And pain killers never seemed to work right. If they even worked at all.

The pain wasn't too bad if I didn't move. And there wasn't much to do in the room. A plain white room with a mirror,so I could see how pathetic I looked,and a TV. Fortunately,this hospital had laptops for the patients and while they were the cheapest ones they could find in a garbage bin because no one wanted them,they did offer access to alternative entertainment.

I whiled away my awake time,which was considerable since I couldn't sleep from the pain,surfing the internet. Poking around in places that are "safe to view in public". And with no family to visit,I was left to the one distraction available to me.

As pages loaded,I wonder what would go first. Heart? Lungs? I really hoped it wouldn't be the liver. Liver failure sounded really slow and painful. I would distract myself with funny videos and comics. Watch whatever abandoned movie property I could watch for free. Leave comments and hope someone could offer me some polite conversation so I wouldn't feel so lonely. And,of course,the occasional troll.

The staff was largely indifferent. They weren't mean or hateful,just didn't want to waste time on an old man circling the drain. Not like I could talk anyway. And my old fingers couldn't really put in things fast enough to use the text to speech function. I'd even downloaded a cartoon voice for it too.

Overall,I just felt,like I had most of my life,like a burden. I'd never really connected with someone enough to start a family and didn't want my kids growing up without a dad. I'd always go where the wind took me and always sought to find my place in the world,but it never really worked out. I'd get bored or distracted and wonder on. I was a lay about my whole life and now all I could do was lay about when I'd rather be doing,well,anything.

I sighed and stared at the ceiling tiles. I noticed the crack between them looked like it had a drip forming. As I watched it form into a drop and begin to fall free,my life ended.

I'd clenched up as the monitors sounded alarms,and then,it was over.
